headline: Approved $15,000 sponsorship for Downtown Stroll 2026; discussed misdirected 2022 invoices for W Pearl design work.
summary: The committee approved $15,000 in sponsorship funding for Downtown Stroll 2026. Nashua PD officers discussed downtown issues including E-bike riders ignoring traffic rules. The committee also discussed invoices from ICON Architecture for W Pearl design work that were mistakenly debited to the DIC account, which Marylou Blaisdell is working with city hall to correct.
decisions: Approved $15,000 for sponsorship of Downtown Stroll 2026, unanimous vote.

decision_evidence.quote: A motion was made by Michael Buckley, seconded by Edward Haynes to approve 15,000 for sponsorship. Unanimous approval.

plain_text:
Minutes 
Downtown Improvement Committee 
September 11, 2026 
Attending: Marylou Blaisdell, Fouad Mahfuz, Edward Haynes, Michael Buckley, Rich Lannan, 
Cole Morgan 
Also, in attendance Alyssa O’Mera – GAD, Alderman Amber Morgan, Officer Joseph Fusco, 
Nashua PD, Sargent Chris Caron PD 
Meeting call to order at 7:50 a.m. 
Discussion Points 
Downtown Stroll 2026 – discussed financial support from the DIC for 2026.  Alyssa O’Mera 
discussed the expected expenses for 2026 and stated sponsorships are beginning.  The 
committee felt it is important that the committee support the stroll.  A motion was made by 
Michael Buckley, seconded by Edward Haynes to approve 15,000 for sponsorship.  Unanimous 
approval. 
Officers of Nashua PD attended to discuss any issues/concerns.  Business owners know the 
downtown officers and receive good responses when issues come up. Dedicated officers 
downtown have made a huge difference.  One issue that was discussed was E bikes downtown 
and the drivers ignoring traffic rules.  
Discussion on invoices debited to DIC account – several invoices from 2022 were debited to the 
DIC account – these invoices were from ICON Architecture for design for W Pearl, the invoices 
are for 25,760, 14,787.20, and two for 3,680.  Marylou stated she is working with city hall to 
resolve this issue and get the account corrected. 
Edward Hayes requested a report from 2021-current of all expenses voted on from this 
committee. 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:55 a.m.
